title: One parcel in two hundred
summary: The depot takes four thousand scans on a weekday morning and refuses about one in two hundred. Scanning the parcel again works. Once a handheld has been refused, every scan on it fails until the app is restarted.

checkpoints.title: A manifest run lists the van's parcels in drop order
checkpoints.hint: A manifest is every parcel with status `at-depot` on that van, in the order `planRunOrder` returns, numbered from 1. A rebuild replaces the lines rather than adding to them, and a van with a `dispatched_at` is not rebuilt at all.

checkpoints.title: A scan taken while a run is planning is accepted, and so is the run
checkpoints.hint: Working out a drop order needs no database, and a transaction held open across it holds the depot's write lock across it too. SQLite runs one writer at a time: while one connection is inside a write transaction, a write on the other is refused rather than queued, and a read that started before that transaction cannot be written on top of afterwards. Read and plan first; open the transaction for the writes only.

checkpoints.title: A scan the depot cannot take is reported and leaves nothing behind
checkpoints.hint: A short write transaction is still a write transaction, so a scan can still arrive inside one, and one day it will. better-sqlite3 throws a `SqliteError` carrying `code` `SQLITE_BUSY` or `SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT`, which is nothing a handheld can act on. Catch that one, throw `DepotBusy`, and let every other error through.

checkpoints.title: A handheld that has been refused takes the next scan
checkpoints.hint: The refused scan wrote nothing, so the retry is a first attempt. What blocks it is the transaction the failed attempt left open on that connection: `db.inTransaction` is still true and the next `BEGIN` fails with "cannot start a transaction within a transaction". `db.transaction(fn)` unwinds on the way out; a hand-written `BEGIN` does not.
